# `unique-items-removed`

uniqueItems removed

| | |
|---|---|
| **Kind** | `wire` |
| **Default severity** | `info` in requests, `warn` in responses |
| **Rule IDs** | `unique-items-removed` (both directions), `unique-items-removed-in-request`, `unique-items-removed-in-response` |
| **Status** | Implemented (M5) |
| **Group** | Schemas ([RULES.md section 7](../../RULES.md)) |

## What it detects

`uniqueItems` was removed.

## Why this default

In requests: more arrays are valid. In responses: clients that treat the array as a set may mis-handle duplicates.

## Example

From test case [`unique-items-removed`](../../test/cases/unique-items-removed/): uniqueItems removed from a response array.

`openapi.yaml`, base → revision:

```diff
  …
            items:
              type: string
-           uniqueItems: true
```

Findings:

- `unique-items-removed-in-response` · warn · #/components/schemas/Pet

## Test cases

The example above is the only test case for this rule.


## Policy options

Every rule takes `severity` (`error`, `warn`, `info` or `off`), `fix` and `explanation` in the policy file, for the generic ID or any variant ID above (the more specific ID wins). The policy file arrives in M6; see [POLICY.md](../../POLICY.md).

```yaml
rules:
  unique-items-removed: warn
```

## How to fix

Keep returning unique items if clients rely on it.
